subject: general
question: Which of the following ratios is the greatest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the ratios to approximate percentages for a quick comparison:

40 : 51 → 40 ÷ 51 ≈ 40 ÷ 50 = 80%

44 : 74 → 44 ÷ 74 ≈ 44 ÷ 75 ≈ 58.6%

42 : 70 → 42 ÷ 70 = 60%

22 : 76 → 22 ÷ 76 ≈ 22 ÷ 75 ≈ 29.3%

**∴ The correct answer is 40 : 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratios: 40 : 51, 44 : 74, 42 : 70, 22 : 76

**Method Used:**

Convert each ratio into a decimal value by dividing the antecedent (first term) by the consequent (second term).

 
• 
 
•

 44 : 74

 ~78.4%

 Comparison of Ratio Percentages

**Calculations:**

⇒ 40 ÷ 51 ≈ 0.784

⇒ 44 ÷ 74 ≈ 0.594

⇒ 42 ÷ 70 = 0.600

⇒ 22 ÷ 76 ≈ 0.289

⇒ Comparing the decimal values: 0.784 > 0.600 > 0.594 > 0.289

⇒ The greatest decimal value is 0.784, which matches the ratio 40 : 51.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 : 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

To rapidly compare two fractions a/b and c/d without decimals, simply multiply diagonally. If a × d > b × c, then the fraction a/b is greater.

Percentage Conversion

Any fraction can be efficiently analyzed by multiplying it by 100 to get a percentage, creating an easily comparable base of 100 for all fractions.

Decimal Approximation

In competitive exams, slightly adjusting the denominator to a nearby round number (like changing 51 to 50) saves crucial time while maintaining relative accuracy.
